key_insight: OxiGen is a crystal diffusion model that explicitly generates oxidation states during sampling to better match real, synthesizable inorganic materials while guaranteeing charge neutrality.
engineering_relevance: For materials discovery pipelines, it improves the realism and validity of generated crystal candidates, making inverse design outputs more useful for downstream screening and synthesis planning.
method: Uses an oxidation-state-aware diffusion model for crystal generation.
Enforces global charge neutrality by construction with a structured output layer.
Performs exact inference over a finite-state automaton to constrain valid oxidation-state assignments.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that OxiGen improves oxidation-state fidelity and achieves the highest rate of stable, unique, and novel crystals among evaluated methods, while maintaining high compositional validity under property conditioning.
watch_item: The approach depends on exact structured inference and oxidation-state annotations, so scalability and performance may be sensitive to the size of the state space and the quality of oxidation-state priors.
